description: Every [PATH-X] and [PATH-X-Y] tagged decision node, extracted from its source file. Each node keeps its original ID so a chosen pattern traces back to source. `node_type: "top_level_pattern"`/`"sub_decision"` nodes are per-template decision-tree branches (settings-pages.md, table-list.md, forms.md, dialogs-and-action-sheets.md, detail-pages.md). `node_type: "cross_cutting_rule"` nodes are binary, checkable rules from permissions-and-conditional-logic.md that apply across templates rather than belonging to one decision tree — `parent` is `null` for these, same as a top-level pattern, since they don't nest under a single PATH. The remaining untagged worked examples and righter-routing call-outs stay in the reference .md files. microcopy-routing.md carries no PATH- tags (it's a routing checklist to the righter skill, not a testable requirement) and is not represented here. pricing-pages.md adds PATH-F (top-level) with PATH-F-* sub-decisions, plus PATH-PRICE-* cross_cutting_rule nodes (U universal, T tier count, S seat, X usage, H hybrid, C consumer).

nodes.condition: User is managing profile, workspace, team, billing, notifications, or members. Multiple related sections that don't need to be edited simultaneously. Changes persist immediately or on explicit save.
nodes.outcome: Use the Settings Page pattern. Depth (shallow vs. deep) is decided by PATH-A-DEPTH-SHALLOW / PATH-A-DEPTH-DEEP. Mobile: sidebar becomes a hamburger menu that slides out and overlaps content.

nodes.condition: 2-3 sections only.
nodes.outcome: Horizontal tabs pinned to top (single page). Structure: page title + tabs + tab content area.

nodes.condition: 4+ sections.
nodes.outcome: Sidebar navigation + sub-pages. Structure: sidebar (pinned on desktop, hamburger on mobile) + main content area.

nodes.condition: User needs to browse, search, filter, and act on multiple items. User occasionally dives into single item details. Bulk actions might be needed.
nodes.outcome: Use the Table/List with Details pattern. Details container: quick edit needed (checkboxes, sliders, dropdowns, a handful of fields) → right sidebar, edit-focused. Viewing details first (default view state, might edit after) → modal, view-focused, with an "Edit" action that navigates to a dedicated form page.

nodes.condition: User is creating a new item, editing an existing item, or completing a workflow/multi-step process.
nodes.outcome: Use the Form pattern. Complexity (simple/medium/complex) is decided by field count via PATH-C-SIMPLE / PATH-C-MEDIUM / PATH-C-COMPLEX.

nodes.condition: 1-6 fields (simple form).
nodes.outcome: Single column, stack vertically. No grouping needed. Space between fields: 24px (spacing-md in vois-tokens).

nodes.condition: 7-15 fields (medium form).
nodes.outcome: Single column OR 2 columns. Group related inputs with section headers (e.g. an address group: street, city, state, zip). Space within section: 24px between fields, 40px between sections.

nodes.condition: 15+ fields OR complex relationships.
nodes.outcome: Tabs OR 2 columns with sections. Group related fields under section headers (e.g. event creation: left = basic info, right = advanced settings).

nodes.condition: Single quick input needed (amount, selection, confirmation). Simple confirmation (yes/no, approve/reject). Dropdown selection, especially on mobile.
nodes.outcome: Desktop: modal dialog, centered, backdrop dims content behind. Mobile: action sheet, slides up from bottom, covers 80-90% screen height for multi-step. Never use an action sheet if text input/keyboard is required — that needs a full modal. Footer button placement: primary right, secondary 20px left of primary, optional tertiary on the left.

nodes.condition: User is viewing a single record in read-only mode. No editing at this level (editing happens on a dedicated form page). User might click through to edit on a separate page.
nodes.outcome: Header: breadcrumb above H1 title, close/back button top right if in a modal. Body: groups of related data stacked vertically, each group as label + value, status indicators/badges where relevant. Actions: no primary action in view-only state; an "Edit" link/button navigates to the form page if editing is available. Mobile: stacked single column, no horizontal grouping.

nodes.rule_name: Hide Page Elements by Role
nodes.condition: User role doesn't have permission to see an element (e.g. non-admin viewing a Members section, non-owner viewing Billing, unpermitted user viewing a Delete account button).
nodes.outcome: Hide the element entirely — it never renders in the DOM. This is deletion, not disabling. Check role at render time; don't render the element at all.

nodes.rule_name: Disable Controls by Permission or Condition
nodes.condition: Content the user cannot update due to an org admin setting or a cascading choice condition (e.g. a workspace admin disabled this setting, the record is archived).
nodes.outcome: Keep the element visible but disabled, in a view-only/disabled state, so the user can visually map the cause/effect relationship. Route the disabled-state explanation (tooltip or helper text) to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Parent/Child Input Dependencies
nodes.condition: A group of related inputs has a conditional relationship — a child input's valid options or availability depend on a parent input's value.
nodes.outcome: Disable the affected child inputs until the parent input is updated/selected with a valid value. Show them disabled but visible, not hidden, so the relationship stays legible. Route the explanation to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Primary Button State
nodes.condition: A form has a primary submit action gated on required fields.
nodes.outcome: The primary button is disabled until all required fields have been filled with valid responses. Route the disabled-state tooltip (e.g. "Fill in all required fields to continue") to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Cascading Accordion/Expansion
nodes.condition: A layout contains multiple expandable/accordion forms.
nodes.outcome: Only one form can remain expanded at a time. Auto-collapse the previously expanded one when the user opens a new one.

nodes.rule_name: Simple Calculation Tables
nodes.condition: A calculation dynamically updates a final value from inline input fields and dropdowns (e.g. quantity × unit price).
nodes.outcome: Use a simple table layout: header row acts as the field label, inline inputs and dropdowns, and never stack more than 4 rows.

nodes.rule_name: Check for a Direct Fit First
nodes.condition: A feature brief names its own product-specific job (e.g. "approval queue", "impersonate a user") rather than one of the five container types.
nodes.outcome: Translate the brief into a plain job-to-be-done and re-check it against the SKILL.md decision tree before assuming it needs new structure. Most briefs that sound novel because of their product-specific name are a direct fit for an existing path once translated.

nodes.rule_name: Combine Existing Patterns Before Inventing a Third
nodes.condition: A brief needs more than one container type's job done at once (e.g. browse-and-approve, multi-step form with a review step, bulk edit from a list).
nodes.outcome: Compose the existing container types that each cover part of the job (e.g. PATH-B + PATH-D for an approval queue; PATH-C + PATH-E for a form with a review step) instead of designing one bespoke hybrid container. If you can't name which existing pattern is doing each part of the job, that's the signal to check PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST instead.

nodes.rule_name: Invent New Structure Only As a Last Resort, and Say So
nodes.condition: The job doesn't fit any existing container type directly (PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST) or as a composition of existing ones (PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE).
nodes.outcome: Build new structure, but name which existing patterns were considered and why they didn't fit — the same reasoning vois_report_pattern_gap asks for, called if available, stated in your own output if not. A new pattern invented this way is a one-off for the brief in front of you, not automatically a new entry in this skill; promoting it to a sixth container type requires the same deliberate review (SKILL.md + patterns-rules.json) every existing path already had.

nodes.rule_name: Dense Layout
nodes.condition: Power user or admin doing this repeatedly; scanning or comparing many rows at once; screen real estate at a premium relative to how much needs to be visible (admin data grids, financial/analytics tables, dashboards, log/audit views).
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the tighter end of the spacing scale (--space-4/-8/-12 between related items), more columns/metrics visible without scrolling, smaller non-body type sizes where DS-TYPOGRAPHY still allows it.

nodes.rule_name: Standard Layout
nodes.condition: Default for most product surfaces — forms, settings pages, typical list/detail views — when neither PATH-DENSITY-DENSE nor PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS's conditions apply.
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the mid spacing scale (--space-16/-24), the values forms.md and settings-pages.md already specify. This is the correct default absent a specific reason to use dense or spacious.

nodes.rule_name: Spacious Layout
nodes.condition: Low-frequency, high-stakes, or attention-focusing moment — onboarding/first-run, empty states, a destructive-confirmation dialog, marketing/landing surfaces, a single critical rarely-seen decision point.
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the looser end of the spacing scale (--space-32/-48 and up), fewer things visible at once, more whitespace around the one thing that matters. Optimize for making one decision unmistakable, not for efficiency.

nodes.condition: User is showing what a product costs and helping a buyer choose a plan. Billing unit is flat, seat-based, usage-based, hybrid, or consumer subscription, with 1 to 4 real tiers.
nodes.outcome: Use the Pricing Page pattern. Billing model picks the sub-decision (PATH-F-FLAT-1 through PATH-F-CONSUMER-PAYWALL). Universal rules (PATH-PRICE-U*) apply to every pricing page. Tier-count rules (PATH-PRICE-T*) apply to layout. Model-specific rules (S, X, H, C) apply per sub-decision.

nodes.condition: Flat price, one plan (no seats, no meter).
nodes.outcome: Single centered card: price with unit and period, 4 to 8 numeric features, one CTA. See PATH-PRICE-T1. Add a small secondary path for large buyers.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, one plan.
nodes.outcome: Single card with per-seat price, included seats, and a seat stepper or input if count changes the price. See PATH-PRICE-T1, PATH-PRICE-S1 to S5.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, 2 to 3 plans.
nodes.outcome: Cards side by side, highlight the middle (or the paid tier when there are 2). Per-seat price with period, included seats, caps disclosed. See PATH-PRICE-T2, T3, S1 to S7.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, 4 plans (Free, Pro, Team, Enterprise).
nodes.outcome: Four cards with short bullets plus a comparison table below. Enterprise shows Custom. Define seat types that bill differently. See PATH-PRICE-T4, S4, S6, U11.

nodes.condition: Usage-based, one plan and one rate.
nodes.outcome: Single card plus an estimator: slider with number input, rate table, itemized total labeled estimated. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X6.

nodes.condition: Usage-based, 2 to 4 plans, each with an included allowance and overage.
nodes.outcome: Plan cards show base price and allowance in the buyer's unit. A calculator below recommends a plan from the input and shows overage separately. See PATH-PRICE-X2, X7, X8.

nodes.condition: Pure pay-as-you-go with no plans.
nodes.outcome: Calculator-first page: slider plus input, live rate table with the active tier highlighted, itemized breakdown, big estimated total, and a note on custom pricing for large volume. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X5, X10, X11.

nodes.condition: Seat fee plus included usage plus overage.
nodes.outcome: Cards show base price and allowance. A calculator (plan, seats, usage, add-ons, total) shows the real bill with monthly and annual totals. See PATH-PRICE-H1 to H4.

nodes.condition: Consumer subscription on a web page (individual, family, student).
nodes.outcome: Selectable plan cards with a clear selected state and one Continue button. Name family plans by accounts or devices. Show monthly equivalent and real charge. See PATH-PRICE-C1, C2, C6.

nodes.condition: Consumer subscription on iOS or in-app paywall.
nodes.outcome: Plan cards, trial timeline, CTA that agrees with post-trial price, Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy. Timing and placement route to conversion-patterns. See PATH-PRICE-C2 to C5, C8, C11.

nodes.rule_name: One lockup for price
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Show price, unit, and billing period together: "$24 per person / month, billed annually." Seen on Descript, Height, Plain. Never split the unit into a footnote.

nodes.rule_name: Annual toggle states its savings
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: "Save 25%," "2 months free," "-20%." Put it next to the toggle, not in a tooltip. Every price on the page must change when the toggle flips. Default to annual only if annual is what you want to sell.

nodes.rule_name: Show the annual total when annual is on
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Copy.ai and Kit both show "$36/mo, billed $432/year." Buyers do the math anyway. Do it for them.

nodes.rule_name: One highlighted tier, never two
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Use a border or elevation plus a short badge ("Most popular," "Recommended"). Do not rely on color alone.

nodes.rule_name: Only the highlighted tier gets the primary button
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Others get secondary style. Descript and Plain do this well. Teachable colors one and blacks the others, which is close but inconsistent when the highlight and the button color disagree.

nodes.rule_name: CTA matches the friction
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Free: "Start free." Paid with trial: "Start free trial." Top tier: "Talk to sales." Do not put "Get started" on every card.

nodes.rule_name: Use "Everything in X, plus:"
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: on every tier above the first. Dub, Height, Windsurf, Circle all do it. It cuts repeated bullets and shows the ladder.

nodes.rule_name: Limits are numbers, not adjectives
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: "30 transcription hours / month" beats "generous limits." Keep to about 6 to 8 bullets per card. If a card runs longer, the extra goes in the comparison table.

nodes.rule_name: "No credit card required" near the free or trial CTA, only when true
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Seen on Dub, Clay, Lyssna.

nodes.rule_name: Enterprise says "Custom" in the price slot
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: List what sales unlocks (SSO, audit logs, dedicated support). Don't invent a starting price you won't honor.

nodes.rule_name: Define any term that changes the bill
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Retool footnotes "standard users" vs "end users." If two things look like seats but bill differently, define both below the cards.

nodes.rule_name: State tax and currency
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Mistral says "excluding taxes" and has a currency switch. Do this if you sell across regions.

nodes.rule_name: Below the cards, in this order:
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: comparison table (3+ tiers), FAQ, reassurance line (cancel anytime, money-back). *Design judgment, not one observed order.*

nodes.rule_name: Mobile stacks cards with the recommended tier first
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: *Design judgment.* Users won't scroll past three tall cards to find the one you want them to see.

nodes.rule_name: One tier
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: One card, centered, price, 4 to 8 features, one CTA. Reflect ("One plan one price") and Skillshare do this. If price varies by a size variable, put the control inside the card (Kit's subscriber dropdown). Add a small secondary path for big buyers ("Request a demo").

nodes.rule_name: Two tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Works best when the split is "me vs us" (Personal / Team) or "free vs paid." Highlight the paid one.

nodes.rule_name: Three tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: The default. Name tiers by audience or stage, not Good/Better/Best. Seen: Hobbyist / Creator / Business (Descript), Launch / Grow / Scale (Plain), Starter / Pro / Enterprise (Current).

nodes.rule_name: Four tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Windsurf, Mistral, Retool, and Firecrawl show four. Only do it when the fourth is a real sales-led tier. Keep card bullets short and put depth in a comparison table. Airtable and Lyssna both use a sticky-header table with grouped sections.

nodes.rule_name: Five or more
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Only for consumer products with distinct benefit stories. Revolut uses five cards with short descriptions and arrows. Klarna uses tabs plus cards. Never a five-column row of feature bullets.

nodes.rule_name: Price per seat per month, with the period
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Plain: "$39 / user / month." Say who counts as a seat.

nodes.rule_name: Show included seats
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Copy.ai: "5 user seats included." Lyssna shows both "included seats" and "maximum seats" per tier.

nodes.rule_name: Add a stepper on the card when seat count changes the price
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Mistral puts "$50/mo, 2 users" with +/- on the Team card. GitBook uses a number input and shows a running total. Show monthly and annual totals.

nodes.rule_name: Separate seat types and say so
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Lyssna has viewer seats. Retool has standard users and end users with different prices. If you have free viewers or cheaper light users, show that as a feature, not fine print.

nodes.rule_name: Disclose caps
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: "Up to 50 members" (Height), "max 15 seats" (Lyssna). Buyers hit these walls later and feel tricked if you hid them.

nodes.rule_name: Volume discounts live on the Enterprise card
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Windsurf: "Volume based annual discounts (>200 seats)."

nodes.rule_name: If the free tier has unlimited seats, say it loudly
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Height and Current lead with "unlimited members." It's a differentiator.

nodes.rule_name: Never show only a per-unit rate
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: A rate like "1.8 cents per charge" is meaningless without a sample bill. Add an estimator (Stripe, Vercel, Cofounder).

nodes.rule_name: Ask in the customer's unit
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Kit asks "How many email subscribers do you have?" Teak asks "Avg. daily active players." Cartesia converts credits to minutes of audio. If your billing unit is abstract (tokens, credits, blocks), translate it. Mailchimp's "blocks of 25,000 emails" is the version to avoid.

nodes.rule_name: Slider plus number input
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Vercel and Grok pair them. The slider is for exploring, the input is for exactness. Label the tick marks.

nodes.rule_name: Show the rate table next to the calculator
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Stripe highlights the active tier under the slider track. Mailchimp shows the full block-rate table. Buyers want to verify your math.

nodes.rule_name: Big estimated total, plus an itemized breakdown
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cofounder lists token, compute, and database costs above a large total. Vercel does the same and adds a comparison. Always label it "estimated."

nodes.rule_name: Default to a realistic value, not zero
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cartesia starts at 45 min. Mailchimp's empty state shows $0.00, which tells the buyer nothing. *My read, not tested.*

nodes.rule_name: Show included allowance and overage separately
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cofounder: "$20 included." Windsurf: "Add-on credits at $10 / 250 credits." Say what happens when they run out.

nodes.rule_name: Recommend a plan from the input
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cartesia shows a "Recommended plan" card after you pick volume. Kit disables tiers that can't cover your count ("Max subscribers reached").

nodes.rule_name: Say what one unit buys
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: If you sell credits, give an example ("1 credit = about 2 pages scraped"). ClassPass explains credits in its own page and notes rollover. Rollover is worth stating.

nodes.rule_name: Offer a reset on multi-input calculators
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Grok has one.

nodes.rule_name: Predictability is a feature
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: If you don't meter something, show it as $0. Agentcard lists "$0 per issued card" and "$0 per order" under a flat monthly fee. If you have a spending cap or pause, say so.

nodes.rule_name: Outcome pricing needs a definition
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Intercom prices Fin at "$0.99 per outcome." Any outcome-based price must define what counts as one, on the same screen.

nodes.rule_name: Show usage per seat
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Windsurf: "500 prompt credits / user / month." Buyers multiply by team size. Put the multiplication in the calculator.

nodes.rule_name: Calculator order follows how buyers think
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Plan, then seats, then usage, then add-ons, then total. GitBook: plan, site count, users, total per month and per year. Teak adds an add-on toggle.

nodes.rule_name: Two totals
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Monthly and annual, always.

nodes.rule_name: Keep the cards simple, put the math in the calculator
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Cards show the base price and allowance. The calculator shows the real bill. Don't cram both into one card.

nodes.rule_name: Plan choice is radio cards with one Continue button
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: MasterClass and Quizlet show cards with a clear selected state and one button below. Do not hide prices behind a tap.

nodes.rule_name: Show both the monthly equivalent and the real charge
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Blue Apron: "$8.33/mo" plus "$99.99/yr." Lifesum shows per-month next to the billing period. Yubo's "$0.60/day" is fine only if the actual charge is also visible.

nodes.rule_name: Explain the trial as a timeline
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Quizlet: today (access), reminder date, trial ends, billing starts. Jomo says "We'll notify you 24h before your trial ends." This is the single clearest trust builder in the set.

nodes.rule_name: The CTA and the small print agree
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: "Start free trial" with "7-day free, then $29.98/year" right under it (Halide). Blue Apron adds a terms checkbox before enabling the button.

nodes.rule_name: iOS: always show Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Jomo, Lifesum, Notion all do.

nodes.rule_name: Name family plans by who's in them
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Deezer: "1 account / 2 accounts / 6 accounts." MasterClass: "1 account, 6 devices."

nodes.rule_name: Free vs Pro list when free is real
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Tide Guide shows a checklist with two columns. It makes the upgrade feel concrete.

nodes.rule_name: Sticky CTAs must not cover a plan
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Tide Guide's button sits over the annual plan card in the screen I saw. Test with the smallest supported device.

nodes.rule_name: Strikethrough anchors only for real prior prices
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Lifesum and Deezer use them. If the higher price was never charged, don't show it. *Ethical rule, not observed.*

nodes.rule_name: One line on why it costs money
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Halide has a "Why is Halide not free?" block. For indie or small-team apps it earns trust.

nodes.rule_name: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`.
